To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a family of diamine sulfates has been synthesized and characterized and used as pH‐biasing agents in preparative‐capillary isoelectric trapping electrophoretic separations of proteins.

we have developed a cost‐effective, high‐yielding synthesis for a family of high‐pH‐buffering capacity, high‐purity, pH‐biased isolelectric buffers, and that these buffers can be successfully employed for preparative‐scale protein separations by pH‐biased isolecule trapping.
we developed a family of high‐performance, high‐buffering‐capacity, low‐pI isoelectric buffers that are useful in pH‐biased isoclectric trapping separations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a family of high‐capacity diamino sulfates for pH‐biased separations, the characterization of the new buffers by CE, ESI‐TOF‐ MS, NMR, and X‐Ray crystallography, and the demonstration of the buffers' utility in pH‐biased isoleucine trapping protein separations.
the development of a new family of isoelectric buffers that can be used in preparative‐level isoelectric trapping CE separations.
the design, synthesis, and application of a family of novel, cost‐effective, high‐buffering‐capacity isoelectric buffers that can be used in pH‐biased isolelectric trapping separations.

the diamino sulfate buffers described here are a family of high‐performance isoelectric buffers that are cost‐effective, and are readily available for the synthesis.
the new buffers are useful for preparative‐scale isoelectric trapping of proteins in the pH range of 5.8‐8.9.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the diamino sulfate is the first pH‐biasing isoelectric buffer with pI in the 5 < pI <8.9 range that is both cost‐effective to synthesize and has the high buffering capacity needed in pH‐biased isocratic separations.

we have developed a family of isoelectric buffers that are suitable for use in preparative‐ and analytical‐scale pH‐biasing separations, and that these buffers have high buffering capacity at their isoelectric pH.
the synthesis of diamine sulfate buffers with high buffering capacity in their isoelectrical state is possible, and the new buffers can be used in pH‐biased isolelectric trapping separations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthesis of isoelectric buffers is a viable alternative to the synthesis of isocratic buffers, especially when the isoelectric buffers are used in a pH biasing role.

the diamino sulfates are excellent pH biasers for pH‐biased IET separations, and that the two generic approaches described here can be used for the synthesis of a wide variety of diamino sulfates, including diamino sulfates that have pI values in a range that is not accessible with the currently available commercial isoelectric buffers. 2016 Wiley Periodicals, Inc.
